caption:
After a weekend of gardening, Mr Turtle's finger catches and clicks every time he makes a fist. It may be what's often called trigger finger.

It happens when a finger tendon doesn't glide smoothly through its tunnel at the base of the finger, and it's often stiffest in the morning. Early on, a few things tend to help: easing off long, hard gripping, padding handles, breaking up tasks, and gentle finger movements in warm water. For some people, a small splint worn overnight can help too.

A finger that locks and won't straighten, or turns hot, red and swollen, needs prompt attention. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can assess your hand. Book online via the link in bio.
